svg.title: SO3 + water to 50 wt% H2SO4 at 140 F on the H–x chart (Btu units)
svg.text: 50 wt% H₂SO₄ at 140 °F from acid and water at 77 °F: points on the H–x chart
H–x diagram for H₂SO₄/H₂O in Btu/lbₘ (Figure for Q 4(a), attached to the paper), redrawn
W: water at 77 °F sits where the 77 °F isotherm meets the x = 0 axis: H_W = 45 Btu/lbₘ.
S: pure H₂SO₄ at 77 °F is the reference state, H_S = 0 at x = 100 %.
M: the straight line W–S at 50 % gives the adiabatic mixture, H_M = 0.5(45.08) = 22.5 Btu/lbₘ.
P: go down the 50 % line to the 140 °F isotherm and across: H_P ≈ −70 Btu/lbₘ (120 °F ≈ −82, 160 °F ≈ −58).
The vertical drop M → P (−92.8 Btu/lbₘ) is the heat removed in the mixing step; blue = 77 °F and 140 °F isotherms.
Redrawn from the chart attached to the paper (digitized; part above ~86 wt% smoothed); in the exam read the printed chart.
